mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand for dwellings, which correlates with increased household spending and equity market optimism, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises above its 3-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 0.5%, it signals a shift towards monetary tightening, increasing discount rates for equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in industrial production (INDPRO) and payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates robust economic expansion, which drives corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO and PAYEMS growth and S&P 500 60-day returns falls below 0.1 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), labor market weakness suppresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales (RSAFS) reflect strong consumer spending, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive equity market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 20-day returns in more than 50% of the time periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI index exceeds 255.0, it indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 255.0.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP (GDPC1) signal sustained economic expansion, which drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint movement of INDPRO and GDPC1 growth fails to predict positive S&P 500 60-day returns in more than 40% of the time periods.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), strong labor market conditions boost consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0%.
